title: C# / .NET
description: Can build C# / .NET services where warnings, cancellation and server-side authorization are enforced — and can write async I/O without blocking on .Result or .Wait.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can write a modern C# console or library with nullable reference types, unit tests, and documented public API choices — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can implement async I/O whose CancellationToken actually cancels, refuse .Result/.Wait on application paths, treat compiler warnings as failures, and add configuration plus structured logging to the solution.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently ship a versioned ASP.NET Core API with server-side authorization, consistent errors that do not leak secrets, integration tests covering auth and transactions, and an OpenAPI document a client can consume.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a failure where a blocked async call, swallowed cancellation, or missing authorization check would look like success, cite the stack or test that proves it, and produce a note another engineer can follow to reproduce the fault without stepping the debugger first.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's C# / .NET service, name a blocked async call, a warning treated as noise, or an authorization check that lives only in the client, and teach when to use a record, DI or a CancellationToken on an unfamiliar codebase.
